practices_evaluation.justification: The method performs a single Act (new Grafo()) and then asserts observable properties. There is one clear Arrange-Act-Assert flow (construct instance, assert properties). No multiple unrelated operations are present.

The test uses only local variables and does not reference or modify shared/static state in the visible code. No @Before/@After are required for this single short test and there is no evidence of inter-test dependencies.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: Only a single happy-path test exists in this class/method; there is no test for an error or exceptional scenario (no assertThrows/@Test(expected=...) or try-catch validating exceptions). Per rules, the class contains only a happy-path test and thus is non-compliant.

The test constructs a Grafo with no input parameters and does not operate on numeric/string input ranges. There are no obvious boundary values to test for this constructor-only happy-path, so boundary analysis is not applicable to this specific method.
The test is short (<10 lines) and self-contained. There is no repeated setup visible that would require helper methods; Given-When-Then comments are used to clarify structure.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test method is small (well under 20 lines) and linear, with no loops or complex conditionals, so complexity is low and the method is focused.

The test contains multiple assertions (not-null, instanceof, toString non-null) that verify multiple observable properties of the constructed object, increasing fault-detection capability beyond a single superficial assertion.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods visible. The test appears active and runnable (uses @Test annotation).
The method Javadoc includes a requirement reference: 'Tests REQ-001', which provides traceability to a requirement ID as required by the practice.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: This is a unit test of object construction with no performance or security assertions. Per decision rules, performance/security testing is typically not applicable for such unit tests unless explicit timing or auth checks are present.

The test method name 'test0' is generic and does not follow descriptive naming conventions (methodName_scenario_expectedResult). Although there is Javadoc, the decision rules prioritize descriptive method names, so this is non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: The class uses EvoSuite artifacts (EvoRunner, EvoAssertions) and the test method name 'test0' is indicative of generated tests (repetitive numeric names). These are signals of heavy code generation and non-minimal/generated naming patterns.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The method includes Given-When-Then comments and a Javadoc referencing a requirement, showing evidence of deliberate design and BDD-style structure that indicates prioritization in design.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test calls public constructor and public methods (toString) and does not access private fields or use reflection. It focuses on observable behavior through public API, so it is maintainable and not tightly coupled to internals.

Assertions include descriptive failure messages and use specific assertion methods (assertNotNull, assertTrue) rather than only generic assertTrue. Most assertions include messages which improves diagnosability.
The test uses concise Given-When-Then inline comments and a descriptive Javadoc; there is no excessive or commented-out code. Comments explain intent rather than restating obvious code.

The test does not use random values, time-based calls, Thread.sleep, or external dependencies in the visible code. It constructs an object deterministically and asserts its properties, so results should be deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test only uses local variables and does not create files, database records, or modify static variables in the visible code; no cleanup is required, so side effects are avoided.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: The class uses @Category(UnitTest.class) at the class level, providing categorization that enables selective execution of unit tests.

Tests should validate inputs at boundaries (min/max/just outside).
Tests should be self-contained and reusable; reuse helper methods/constants.

practices_report.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_report.description: Keep test cases small and avoid unnecessary complexity like loops/conditionals.
Use comprehensive assertions verifying multiple properties to detect faults.
Avoid @Ignore/@Disabled and commented-out tests; keep tests active.
Link tests to requirements via annotations or Javadoc.

practices_report.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_report.description: Performance and security tests should be separate and explicit.
Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome.

practices_report.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation

practices_report.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design

practices_report.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
